article.title: Issue 63: The Internet Speaks
article.content: Our Line Is Left-Zinovievism With American CharacteristicsHonestly the fundamental problem with Jacobin is that it doesn’t seem willing to have an actual editorial line instead of credulously featuring everybody willing to talk about whatever beliefs they have in “left-wing” language lol. — @OttokarHochmanMan-to-Man Defense Is Bourgeois IndividualismJacobin magazine youth basketball camp. — @ydsTreyWe Actually Publish in Six, Soon to Be Seven, LanguagesWhy is Germany the only country with a dedicated Jacobin magazine? Is there no demand for French Jacobin? Polish Jacobin? Mexican Jacobin? — @DirteeerMartiniBrand Consistency MattersAre people really surprised a magazine called Jacobin would publish an article praising a bourgeois revolution? Do they know who the Jacobins were? — @secondbyfarceIn Defense of GolfI think people think I’m kidding when I say that every article Jacobin publishes these days follows the same pattern: “Here’s why an aspect of bourgeois society universally rejected by socialists is actually good and potentially revolutionary.” I’m really not. — @Reverend_BanjoLeft-Wing HegemonyTrying to decide whether to read the Nation article about how Hamilton is bad or the Jacobin article about how Hamilton is bad. — @d_h_sandersWe’ve Accepted Worse PitchesMy favorite kind of Jacobin article is the one that connects something completely bizarre to socialism, like “How We Can Make Astrology Proletarian” or “The Subtle Leninism of AI fruit love island.” — @souljagoytellerOnly After the Karl-Anthony Towns SymposiumBracing for the “Jalen Brunson Is a Socialist” Jacobin article. — @NuclearWomprat
